text: dsh-cost-gate 是一个接入 DeepSeek Harness 的模型支出控制插件，在 llm/stream 调用链上先检查预算，再放行模型请求，并在返回 usage 数据时累计费用。它按部署、会话或配置的用户范围记录支出，支持日、月和总额周期；达到软阈值后可切换到指定模型，达到上限时可阻止请求，也可用 dryRun 只记录决策。账本可选写入本地文件。适合需要限制 DSH 模型调用成本并按范围归集支出的部署。源码未要求额外 API key；费率由配置提供。

dsh-cost-gate meters DSH model-call spend at the llm/stream boundary. It can block calls at a configured limit, switch models after a soft threshold, and record usage by deployment or session. Rates and limits are supplied in plugin configuration.
想给 DSH 的模型调用设月度费用上限，超出后自动拦截。
模型花费快到预算时，能不能自动换成便宜的模型？
I need DSH to stop model requests once a spending cap is reached.
dsh-cost-gate 的功能「预算门控」：每次模型请求前检查累计支出，按预算放行、切换模型或阻止调用，并依据返回的 usage 和配置费率更新账本。

dsh-cost-gate README · dsh-cost-gate：**Spend enforcement for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — not another dashboard.**

The dsh ecosystem has plenty of cost plugins. Every one of them *measures*:
ledgers, statistics, heatmaps, balance widgets. They tell you what you spent
**after you spent it**.

This one **stops the call**.

dsh-cost-gate README · dsh-cost-gate：```
        ┌─ over budget? ──> throw, before a single token is billed
llm/stream waterfall ─┼─ past 80%? ────> silently route to the cheap model
        └─ fine? ────────> pass through, then meter the usage chunk
```

`llm/stream` is a cordis **waterfall** — the decision happens *before* `next()`
runs, which is the only place enforcement can actually work.

dsh-cost-gate README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:frozo-ai/dsh-budget   # npm: dsh-cost-gate
```

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: budget
      name: 'dsh-cost-gate/plugin'
      config:

Set `dryRun: true` to log decisions without blocking — roll out safely, then
turn it on.

dsh-cost-gate README · Design notes：**Integer micro-dollars.** Costs accumulate as integers, never floats. A test
runs 10,000 calls and asserts zero drift, because this decides whether people
get blocked.

**Cache tokens are disjoint.** Per dsh's `TokenUsage` contract, `cacheRead` and
`cacheWrite` are *not* included in `inputTokens`, so they're added at their own
rates rather than folded in.

**Atomic ledger writes.** Temp file plus rename — a torn write must not lose
budget state.

dsh-cost-gate README · Design notes：**UTC period boundaries**, so a daily budget resets at a time everyone agrees on.

**Fails open, deliberately.** No `limitUsd` means metering only. Enforcement is
opt-in: a budget plugin that accidentally blocks your whole team is worse than
one that doesn't block at all.

dsh-cost-gate README · Related work：[`PerryLink/dsh-budget`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-budget) covers similar
ground — metering, caps, alerts, carbon estimates, a Settings tab. If you want
dashboards and reporting, look there first. This plugin is narrower on purpose:
it gates the `llm/stream` waterfall so an over-budget call is refused *before*
it is billed, and does little else.

dsh-cost-gate README · Attribution：```yaml
scopeBy: session          # deployment (default) | session | user
perScopeLimitUsd:
  'system:compaction': null    # unlimited — overhead must never block the agent
  'user:alice': 100

**`session`** uses `GenerateOptions.sessionId`, which dsh genuinely provides.

dsh-cost-gate README · Attribution：**`user`** needs a mapping dsh cannot supply — there is no user identity at the
llm seam. So it is given, never guessed:
- `userEnv: 'DSH_USER'` — one dsh instance per user
- `sessionUsers: { <sessionId>: 'alice' }` — an operator-supplied map

An unattributable call lands in `user:unattributed`. It is never charged to
whoever happens to be handy — a chargeback report that invents attributions is
worse than one that admits gaps.

dsh-cost-gate README · Attribution：**System overhead is separated.** Compaction and session-title calls carry a
`purpose` and are billed to `system:*`, so background work can never exhaust a
person's budget. Give them a `null` limit so they cannot be blocked.

dsh-cost-gate README · Known limitations：- **Per-user requires operator setup** — see Attribution above. dsh has no user
  concept at the llm seam, so nothing can infer it.
- **Unknown models price as $0** rather than crashing. Add them to `rates`.
- Pricing tables are yours to maintain; providers change rates.

dsh-cost-gate README · Test：```sh
npm test   # 29 checks: pricing, drift, periods, durability, decisions, attribution
```
